method: Read all25 current complete items and prior findings, including keys, explanations, takeaway and metadata. Rechecks are anchored to a frozen snapshot; all status decisions are manually reasoned.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Tongue swelling/voice change during ramipril use threatens airway even without rash or after months of treatment; emergency response precedes oral therapy or future-dose planning.
Stable pulmonary observations and onset after ACE inhibitor initiation support medication review. A dry cough alone does not establish infection or congestion; foundation label is appropriate.

Potassium4.8 before a new concentrated potassium source cannot predict safety with spironolactone. Dose spacing does not remove potassium retention, and annual follow-up would not address the proposed change.

New bradycardia, gastrointestinal/visual symptoms and renal decline form a coherent digoxin-toxicity concern. Withholding pending urgent rhythm/toxicity assessment fits scope and the current deterioration; last week’s level cannot exclude it.

Muscle pain/weakness plus dark urine on statin therapy require prompt muscle/renal assessment. Lipid testing, food administration and exercise do not address this potentially serious adverse-effect pattern.

Same-day sildenafil exposure contraindicates nitrate despite an acceptable initial pressure. Urgent chest-pain review supplies a safe alternative plan; no unverified washout interval or partial dose is prescribed.

Reduced oedema with stable standing pressure and less breathlessness at equal activity demonstrate benefit. Orthostatic faintness, rising oxygen requirement and potassium depletion prevent classifying diuresis alone as success.
Confusion with sodium124 is symptomatic marked hyponatraemia needing urgent assessment before further thiazide. Extra free water or dosing based solely on pressure could worsen the problem.
Controlled angina may reflect metoprolol efficacy and does not justify abrupt withdrawal or an improvised taper/PRN schedule. Foundation label is appropriate.

options: Help the client sit or lie safely and reassess symptoms
Report the positional readings for regimen review
Reassure because the supine pressure is normal
Give a large glass of water and repeat the standing measurement immediately
Give the next scheduled dose if the supine pressure has returned to baseline
why: Positioning limits immediate fall risk during symptomatic pressure reduction.
The measurable symptomatic change can guide treatment adjustment.
A normal supine reading does not explain away postural instability.
A fluid trial does not take priority over safe positioning in a symptomatic client; fluid suitability and reassessment timing require the clinical context.
Supine recovery does not resolve the symptomatic postural fall or replace review of the regimen.

items.assessment: Earlier planned timing directly addresses nocturia from22:00furosemide while retaining prescribed treatment; reduced dose, daytime restriction and ad hoc symptom dosing change other aspects of care.

Day-six platelet fall>50% with new thrombosis is a coherent HIT pattern. Stop heparin/escalate under protocol rather than reduce its dose or await routine review. Targeted Thrombosis Canada evidence corroborates stopping all exposure.
Urgent anticoagulated head-injury assessment is correct, but “consider the injury managed” makes option1 an overtly careless caricature. Replace it with a realistic delayed-review plan.
issues: Urgent anticoagulated head-injury assessment is correct, but “consider the injury managed” makes option1 an overtly careless caricature. Replace it with a realistic delayed-review plan.

options: Check INR before deciding whether assessment is needed
Hold the next apixaban dose and arrange review at tomorrow’s clinic
Arrange urgent head-injury assessment and follow the escalation pathway
Continue usual checks unless a headache develops
why: INR does not reliably measure apixaban's anticoagulant effect.
A dose decision does not evaluate possible intracranial injury, and delaying assessment is not justified by initially normal neurological findings.
Early normal findings do not exclude anticoagulant-associated intracranial bleeding.
Waiting for symptoms may delay recognition of occult bleeding.

items.assessment: Melena with dizziness during clopidogrel use calls for circulation assessment and urgent bleeding review, rather than a screening test, constipation advice or delayed administration/reporting.

The clinical key appropriately integrates drug, renal function and procedure. Asking the client to choose between bleeding and clotting is an implausibly unsupported alternative; use a generic interruption-schedule error.
issues: The clinical key appropriately integrates drug, renal function and procedure. Asking the client to choose between bleeding and clotting is an implausibly unsupported alternative; use a generic interruption-schedule error.

options: Obtain a plan incorporating the drug, renal function and procedure
Use the interruption schedule from a different anticoagulant
Continue because the latest INR is normal
Apply the standard24-hour interruption in the clinic’s general preparation handout
why: These factors affect interruption and restart decisions.
Drug-specific elimination and bleeding risk differ.
A normal INR does not establish absent direct-anticoagulant effect.
A generic interval may not account for this drug, new renal decline and the procedure’s bleeding risk; an individualized plan is required.

items.assessment: Soft oral care and checking nonprescription NSAIDs are appropriate bleeding precautions. Automatic doubling, INR-directed dosing for unspecified anticoagulant and interruption for every bruise are recognizable anticoagulation misconceptions; the key does not supply a universal missed-dose schedule.
Both monitoring distractors use “only,” signalling incompleteness instead of requiring comparison of monitoring plans.
issues: Both monitoring distractors use “only,” signalling incompleteness instead of requiring comparison of monitoring plans.

options: Keep a daily record of visible bruises to guide follow-up
Arrange a safety review when the prescribed dose is changed
Bleeding, kidney function and medication changes still need review
Ask for weekly INR tests to confirm effectiveness
why: Bruise tracking may help, but important bleeding can be internal and other exposure-related risks still need follow-up.
Dose changes matter, but renal function, bleeding and interactions can change at an unchanged dose.
Absence of routine INR titration does not eliminate safety monitoring.
INR is not used to routinely titrate apixaban.

items.assessment: Pressure78/44 with faintness after nitrate is acute circulatory instability despite less chest pain. Rapid confirmation may accompany response but should not postpone escalation; another dose or routine-interval reassessment is inappropriate.
The intended volume interpretation is sound, but “no further assessment” overtly flags the negative option. Use a competing physiological interpretation.
issues: The intended volume interpretation is sound, but “no further assessment” overtly flags the negative option. Use a competing physiological interpretation.

options: Possible intravascular depletion despite reduced edema
Persistent fluid overload because some ankle edema remains
Expected fluid mobilization with adequately preserved circulating volume
A need to increase diuretic frequency
why: Improved congestion can coexist with excessive circulating-volume loss.
Residual peripheral edema does not exclude depleted circulating volume.
Dry mouth and symptomatic postural change argue against assuming that circulating volume remains adequate merely because lung sounds cleared.
More diuresis may worsen the symptoms of depletion.

items.assessment: New amlodipine-related oedema is plausibly supported, but permanent medication cessation is a weak extreme. Use a plausible symptom-management plan that delays needed medication review.
issues: New amlodipine-related oedema is plausibly supported, but permanent medication cessation is a weak extreme. Use a plausible symptom-management plan that delays needed medication review.

options: Delay reporting until breathlessness develops
Assess and report possible medication-related peripheral edema
Request an automatic diuretic increase for heart failure
Start leg elevation and compression and reassess at the next routine visit
why: A medication adverse effect can warrant review before respiratory compromise.
The timing and absence of pulmonary symptoms support reviewing amlodipine.
The assessment does not establish systemic congestion as the cause.
Local measures may be considered, but a new dose-related change should be assessed and communicated rather than managed as established benign oedema.

items.assessment: Diltiazem and metoprolol both slow rate/conduction; near-syncope at42/min requires withholding pending urgent assessment. Selecting one on class name or recency does not resolve the combined risk.

proposedChanges.stem: A client has started ramipril while continuing prescribed hydrochlorothiazide. Which pairs should be included in the planned medication-safety follow-up? Select all that apply.
options: Creatinine and serum potassium trends
Prothrombin time and INR trends
Hearing acuity and vestibular function
Serum amylase and lipase trends
Blood pressure and postural symptoms
why: Renal function and potassium can change after ACE inhibitor initiation, particularly when volume status is changing.
These measure coagulation and are not routine indicators of the stated ACE inhibitor effects.
These assessments target possible ototoxicity in other treatment contexts, rather than the stated ACE inhibitor effects.
Pancreatic enzymes do not monitor the stated renal, potassium or haemodynamic effects.
Combined therapy can produce clinically important hypotension, including symptomatic postural changes.

items.assessment: Some alternatives are actions rather than explanations, and one says chest symptoms need no action. Use parallel explanations of the planned interval to remove that giveaway.
issues: Some alternatives are actions rather than explanations, and one says chest symptoms need no action. Use parallel explanations of the planned interval to remove that giveaway.

options: The interval helps preserve the response to subsequent nitrate exposure
The interval is mainly intended to let the previous application site recover
The interval makes up for slower nitrate absorption while the client is asleep
The interval compensates for the kidneys retaining nitrate between applications
why: Continuous nitrate exposure can produce tolerance, so a prescribed nitrate-free interval helps maintain responsiveness.
Skin-site rotation and skin assessment matter, but preventing tolerance is the main purpose of the prescribed nitrate-free interval.
The interval is not prescribed because normal sleep makes nitrate absorption too slow.
The standard planned interval addresses tolerance, not an assumed renal-clearance problem.

options: Arrange financial assistance as the first step
Set a reminder alarm for the same clock time each day
Develop a feasible prescribed schedule with the client and team
Review how consistent therapy reduces the long-term risk of stroke
